In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new recombinant strain for bioremediation purposes.
the improvement of the biotechnological potential of P. chryssoprium by the expression of different lignin-degrading oxidoreductive enzymes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
P. chrysospirium is able to produce laccases and their expression can be increased by genetic modification.
the co-expression of lccases with peroxidases is possible in P. chryssoporium and that this co-expression improves the degradation of phenolics and non-phenolics substrates.
P. chrysosporum can be transformed with laccase genes, but that it is not possible to express laccases at levels similar to those found in other basidiomycetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the co-expression of four different oxidoreductases (two laccases, a manganese peroxidase, and a lignin peroxidases) in the same recombinant strain of P. chryso-sporium.
the co-expression of four different oxidoreductases improves the biodegradation of different lignin-related compounds.
the co-overexpression of four ligninolytic enzymes in P. chysosporium is possible and the resulting transformant strains showed an improved biodegradation of phenolic and synthetic dyes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the four enzymes, LiP, MnP, VP, and Lac, can be constitutely expressed in a single strain of P. chysosporium, and the co-expressed enzymes can degrade both phenolic and non phenolic compounds.

the expression of the four oxidoreductase genes in P. chryssoporium is possible and that the co-expression of these enzymes improves the ability of the fungus to degrade phenolic and nonphenolic compounds.

the expression of the four enzymes in a single transform of P. chryosporium is possible, and that the co-expression of lccases and peroxidase in a single transform is an efficient way to improve the degradation of a broad range of phenolic and/or non-phenolic compounds.
